messages:
Deborah: Quick heads-up — rolling out two billing changes on Monday (2026-04-06) that affect quotas and invoice layout. Please read and share with your teams.

Deborah: Summary: 1) quota tiering (new bucketed limits + soft/strict behavior), 2) simplified invoice CSV and machine-friendly line items, 3) sunsetting of legacy promotional credits for accounts created before 2023-01-01. Full doc: https://docs.redwood.example/billing/quota-tiering-invoice-update

Cameron: thanks — can you call out what "soft/strict" means?

Deborah: Sure — soft = we allow short microbursts above quota (rate-limited with 429 backoff after Xs) while logging and alerting; strict = immediate throttling for the route with no burst. Default for free/prod-tier will be soft; higher committed tiers can opt into strict via contract.

Lisa: what about Dedicated/Private customers? any changes to reserved capacity SLAs?

Deborah: No SLA changes. Dedicated/Private customers keep their contracted quotas. The tiering config only applies to hosted accounts. For Dedicated we will surface the same CSV invoice format but leave usage semantics untouched.

Ryan: ops note — we'll instrument a new header on responses so apps can detect soft-burst vs throttled responses: X-Quota-State: soft|strict and X-Quota-Remaining. Plan: rollout runtime flag + feature flip on Monday.

Ryan: example header:```
X-Quota-State: soft
X-Quota-Remaining: 42
```

SupportBot: Notice scheduled: support will auto-send the FAQ link and a templated response to accounts hitting new bucket thresholds. Template: https://internal.redwood/support/templates/quota-tiering-faq

Emma: Legal and Compliance reviewed the invoice changes. We confirmed the simplified CSV still includes line-level product codes and tax breakdowns. No regulatory blockers.

Deborah: Overage policy tweak: instead of a fixed 48-hour grace window we now have a per-customer configurable grace period up to 7 days (default 72 hours). This helps teams with predictable billing while avoiding surprise cutoffs. Ops will surface this in the billing UI.

Ops: noted — UI changes will be behind a rollout flag. We'll post a changelog entry and a short screencast in #announcements once it's live.

Cameron: will there be automated credits applied for customers who lose access to legacy promo credits?

Deborah: For affected accounts we will provide a one-time pro-rated credit equal to the remaining promotional balance (see migration plan in doc). We will email impacted customers 7 days before enforcement and include a one-click migration action in the billing portal.

Lisa: any impact to rate limits for embedding-heavy workloads?

Ryan: Rate limit tiers stay same, but we added a microburst allowance for short embedding spikes on the Developer and Scale tiers. If a job consistently exceeds the microburst allowance, it moves the customer into the bucketed quota checks and will surface recommendations (batching, caching, quantization suggestions).

SupportBot: FYI — new support tag: billing-quota-tiering. Use it when filing cases about unexpected 429s after rollout.

Deborah: Action items: 1) Eng to flip runtime flag Monday AM (Ryan) 2) Support to prepare canned responses (Support) 3) Product/Design to enable billing UI toggle and email templates (Lisa) 4) Finance to validate CSV export samples (Emma) 5) Ops to publish changelog + screencast (Ops).

Ryan: I'll post a short runbook in #eng-runtime with detection thresholds and mitigation steps.

Cameron: thanks — please ping #customer-success once the email batch goes out so we can prep CS for inbound.

Deborah: Will do. If you have immediate questions, DM me or drop them here. :wave:
